steps.situation: A caller says he is from the company that makes the clinic's billing software: "Your licence ends today. Please install AnyDesk so I can renew it for you." He is polite and knows the clinic's name.

front_desk.text: Install it: he knows our clinic, so he must be genuine
front_desk.feedback: Anyone can find a clinic's name online. Real companies don't ask you to install things on a surprise call.

front_desk.text: Say you'll call back, hang up, and call the number saved in ShieldMate
front_desk.feedback: Right. Call back on a number you already have, never one the caller gives you.

front_desk.text: Ask him for his number so you can call him back
front_desk.feedback: A number from the caller goes straight back to the scammer. Use the one saved in ShieldMate.

billing.text: Tell Meena to go ahead: keeping the billing software running matters
billing.feedback: The software can wait two minutes. Check first.

billing.text: Tell Meena to hang up and check with the saved IT contact first
billing.feedback: Right. One call to a number you already have tells you if it's real.

steps.situation: Earlier this week someone did install it. Now the mouse on the reception computer is moving by itself and the billing screen is open.

front_desk.text: Switch the computer off at the wall
front_desk.feedback: Switching off loses evidence IT needs. Pull out the network cable instead and leave it on.

front_desk.text: Pull out the network cable (or turn Wi-Fi off) and leave the computer on
front_desk.feedback: Right. With the cable out, they can't control it any more, and the evidence stays.

front_desk.text: Watch what they do so you can tell IT later
front_desk.feedback: Every second it is connected, they can open more. Cut the network first.

billing.text: Stop using the reception computer and tell Dr. Rao
billing.feedback: Right. Keep off it and make sure the owner knows.

billing.text: Check the bank account on your phone using the same password
billing.feedback: If they watched that password being typed, they have it too. Wait for IT.

owner.text: Call the saved IT contact and ask them to remove the program
owner.feedback: Right. IT removes the program and checks what else it touched.

owner.text: Call the number the caller gave and ask them to stop
owner.feedback: That number is the scammer's. Only use contacts saved in ShieldMate.

steps.situation: The caller rings back: "To finish the renewal, read me the OTP code that just came to your phone."

front_desk.text: Read out the code: it's only to finish the renewal
front_desk.feedback: An OTP code is a key to a bank account or email. Nobody genuine ever asks you to read one out.

front_desk.text: Hang up. Never share an OTP code, and tell Dr. Rao
front_desk.feedback: Right. Hanging up is never rude when someone asks for a code.

billing.text: Keep using online banking as usual: the cable is out now
billing.feedback: They may already have the banking password. Change it from a different computer first.

billing.text: Call the bank to stop any payments, then change the banking password from a different computer
billing.feedback: Right. The bank can hold payments while the password is changed somewhere safe.

owner.text: Plug the network cable back in now that the caller has gone
owner.feedback: Wait until IT has removed the program, or they can connect again.

owner.text: Change every password typed on the reception computer, from a different device
owner.feedback: Right. Anything typed there may have been seen.

steps.situation: IT has removed the program. Nobody is sure what the caller looked at.

staff.text: Write down the caller's number, the times, and what he asked for, and give it to Dr. Rao
staff.feedback: Right. Those details are what the report needs.

staff.text: Forget about it: IT has fixed it
staff.feedback: Fixed isn't the end. Write it down while you remember it.

owner.text: Don't report: no money was lost
owner.feedback: Someone controlled a clinic computer that can open patient records. That must be reported, even with no money lost.

owner.text: Report the scam on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in, and to CERT-In within 6 hours
owner.feedback: Right. Reporting helps stop the same caller tricking the next clinic.
